title: Functions Triggers
description: Learn what triggers are in Azure Functions and explore the most commonly used trigger types.

data.text: A trigger is the event that causes an Azure Function to run. Each function must have exactly one trigger. The trigger defines how the function is invoked and provides the function's input data.
Triggers are defined using attributes in code and configured in the function.json or host.json file.

Authorization Levels
data.text: HTTP triggers support authorization levels: Anonymous (no key needed), Function (function key required), and Admin (master key required). Choose the strictest level your scenario needs.

data.title: Create a Timer Trigger Function
data.description: Create an Azure Function with a Timer trigger that runs every 5 minutes and logs a message. Test it locally using Azure Functions Core Tools.
steps: Create a new function with `func new --template "Timer Trigger" --name LogTimer`
Modify the CRON expression to `0 */5 * * * *` (every 5 minutes)
Run `func start` and verify the log output
data.expectedOutcome: The function fires every 5 minutes and logs to the console.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: A trigger is the event that starts a function
Each function has exactly one trigger
Common triggers include HTTP, Timer, Blob, and Queue
AuthorizationLevel controls who can invoke HTTP triggers
data.takeaway: Triggers define when and how your function runs.
